label: Institution
name: Apostolic United Brethren
summary:
The Apostolic United Brethren (AUB), founded in 1951 as a breakaway from the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (FLDS) — is the second-largest fundamentalist Mormon group in North America, practicing polygamy (plural marriage) as a religious obligation based on the original 19th-century teachings of Joseph Smith and Brigham Young that were officially discontinued by the LDS Church in 1890. The AUB is based primarily in Bluffdale, Utah, and the Rocky Mountain region, with thousands of members.

Fundamentalist Mormon polygamy is one of the most persistent and legally complex religious minority practices in American history: despite the 1890 LDS manifesto formally suspending polygamy (issued under extreme US government pressure including anti-polygamy laws, the seizure of Church property, and threatened disenfranchisement of Utah Territory), various Mormon fundamentalist groups have maintained polygamy as a religious practice, believing the 1890 manifesto was an impermissible capitulation to government coercion that violated divine revelation.

The AUB, unlike the more publicly controversial FLDS led by Warren Jeffs, has generally maintained a lower profile and been more open to outsider contact. The group was brought to national attention through the reality television series 'Sister Wives,' which followed an AUB family, bringing rare sympathetic public exposure to the fundamentalist Mormon polygamy community. The AUB's legal status in the US remains complex — polygamy is technically illegal in all states, but prosecutorial practice has varied.
